code_label: Quantum self-attention reimplemented inside QNN
text_span: We propose a QNN-SAM model that incorporates SAM functionalities within the Quantum Neural Network (QNN) algorithm.
locator: A B S T R A C T
rationale: States the paper’s central proposed model and integration goal.

code_label: No QRAM or auxiliary qubits required
text_span: This model exclusively employs Parameterized Quantum Circuits (PQCs), eliminating the necessity for QRAM or auxiliary qubits.
locator: A B S T R A C T
rationale: Key design decision emphasizing resource reduction and NISQ suitability.

code_label: Built for NISQ devices
text_span: It is tailored for Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices.
locator: A B S T R A C T
rationale: Explicit deployment target for the proposed model.

code_label: Query key value quantum states defined
text_span: The QNN-SAM model defines three quantum states—query, key, and value quantum states.
locator: A B S T R A C T
rationale: Core representational choice for the attention mechanism.

code_label: Quantum interference used for focusing
text_span: Leveraging the principle of quantum interference, PQC with quantum focusing function has been constructed.
locator: A B S T R A C T
rationale: Describes the mechanism used to implement attention focusing.

code_label: Attention score and weight computed with PQCs
text_span: The QNN-SAM model calculates the attention score and attention weight between query and key quantum states only using PQCs.
locator: A B S T R A C T
rationale: Summarizes the fully quantum attention computation.

code_label: Superior performance across tasks
text_span: This model demonstrated superior complexity, convergence, and accuracy in predicting meteorological indicators, stock price prediction and classifying text.
locator: A B S T R A C T
rationale: High-level performance claim across all evaluated tasks.

code_label: Meteorological task parameter reduction and accuracy
text_span: the QNN-SAM model required only one-fourth of the SAM parameters while achieving high accuracy rates of 99.87 %, 93.51 %, and 92.54 %.
locator: A B S T R A C T
rationale: Quantified result for the meteorological prediction task.

code_label: Stock prediction metrics improved
text_span: For stock price prediction, this model yielded higher R² values and lower MAPE and RMSE metrics.
locator: A B S T R A C T
rationale: Summarizes comparative stock prediction performance.

code_label: Text classification parameter reduction and accuracy
text_span: text classification tasks also benefited from the model, which utilized one-third of the baseline parameters and achieved accuracy rates up to 74.19 % on RP task.
locator: A B S T R A C T
rationale: Quantified result for the text classification task.

code_label: Noise robustness demonstrated
text_span: the robustness of QNN-SAM against various typical types of quantum noise is demonstrated
locator: A B S T R A C T
rationale: Claims robustness under common quantum noise models.

code_label: Meteorological dataset and forecasting setup
text_span: The dataset comprises three key indicators: atmospheric pressure, temperature, and relative humidity.
rationale: Defines the first experimental dataset and prediction target.

code_label: Forecasting uses prior days to predict the fifth day
text_span: The objective is to train QNN-SAM model to forecast the value of each indicator on the fifth day based on data from the preceding four days.
rationale: States the task formulation for meteorological prediction.

code_label: Meteorological preprocessing by differencing and normalization
text_span: The dataset was preprocessed through differencing and normalization.
rationale: Records the preprocessing choice for the numerical task.

code_label: Meteorological accuracy and parameter comparison
text_span: QNN-SAMb and QNN-SAMo models consistently achieve accuracies of 90 % or higher across all indicators
rationale: Summarizes the main meteorological performance outcome.

code_label: QNN-SAMo converges better than QNN-SAMb
text_span: QNN-SAMo exhibits higher prediction accuracy, as shown in Table 2, and better convergence characteristics, as illustrated in Fig. 5.
rationale: Comparative result favoring the QNN-SAMo variant.

code_label: Removing redundant inputs improves learning dynamics
text_span: removing redundant input features not only simplifies the QNN-SAM architecture by reducing parameter complexity but also improves learning dynamics by minimizing noise in Hilbert space.
rationale: Analytical observation linking simplification to better optimization.

code_label: Text datasets MC and RP defined
text_span: The second task involves binary text classification using two public datasets, i.e., the MC and RP synthetic dataset.
rationale: Defines the second experimental setting.

code_label: RP is harder due to sparse vocabulary
text_span: the size of vocabulary and the sparseness of words make this task more challenging than the MC task.
rationale: States a task difficulty observation.

code_label: Text classification uses word embedding via encoding circuit
text_span: we use the encoding circuit Ue(xi) for word embedding to obtain the corresponding Query, Key and Value quantum states.
rationale: Describes how text inputs are represented in the model.

code_label: MC perfect classification
text_span: On the MC task, both QNN-SAMb and QNN-SAMo achieved perfect classification accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score of 100 %.
rationale: Reports the strongest text-classification result on MC.

code_label: RP performance exceeds quantum baselines
text_span: the accuracy of QNN-SAM outperformed the quantum baseline model by 3.23–6.45 %age points, reaching 70.97 % and 74.19 % respectively.
rationale: Quantifies improvement over baseline on RP.

code_label: Parameter efficiency on RP
text_span: QNN-SAM model require only 50 % of the trainable parameters (72–88 vs. 25–168) on RP task compared to the quantum baseline models.
rationale: Highlights parameter savings in the text task.

code_label: QSANN is hybrid while QNN-SAM is fully quantum
text_span: the QSANN model is a quantum-classical hybrid
rationale: Clarifies the distinction between the compared models.

code_label: Stock dataset contains 12 stocks and six indices
text_span: The dataset comprises 12 stocks sourced from Yahoo Finance
rationale: Defines the stock prediction dataset.

code_label: Stock task predicts next-day closing price from prior four days
text_span: The objective of stock price prediction is to forecast the closing price for the following day using the indices data from the preceding four days.
rationale: States the stock forecasting task formulation.

code_label: Stock results favor QNN-SAM over SAM
text_span: In the majority of cases involving companies such as AAPL, AMGN, BA, CAT, CSCO, HD, KO, JNJ, JPM, MMM, and MSFT, both QNN-SAMo and QNN-SAMb exhibit higher R² values than SAM.
rationale: Summarizes comparative stock prediction performance.

code_label: QNN-SAMo usually slightly better than QNN-SAMb
text_span: QNN-SAMo exhibited slightly superior performance compared to QNN-SAMb across the majority of stocks.
rationale: Comparative result between the two variants.

code_label: Performance varies by stock characteristics
text_span: the model’s performance is not solely dependent on the model itself but is also notably impacted by the distinct characteristics of the particular stock being predicted.
rationale: Analytical observation about task dependence.

code_label: Noise experiment uses five common channels
text_span: We examine five common types of quantum noise: bit-flip, depolarizing noise, amplitude-damping, phase flip, and phase damping
rationale: Defines the robustness evaluation setup.

code_label: Noise impact depends on type and dataset
text_span: the impact of noise depends on both the type of noise and the dataset being used.
rationale: Summarizes the main robustness finding.

code_label: RP is more vulnerable to noise
text_span: for the RP dataset, accuracy decreases with higher noise levels.
rationale: Identifies the most noise-sensitive dataset.

code_label: Bit-flip and amplitude damping are more harmful
text_span: bit-flip, depolarizing noise and amplitude damping noise have a stronger impact than phase flip and phase damping.
rationale: Ranks the relative severity of noise types.

code_label: Zero-noise extrapolation and randomized compilation suggested
text_span: For depolarizing and bit flip noise, the Zero-Noise Extrapolation (ZNE) method effectively suppresses noise.
rationale: Mentions mitigation methods for noisy hardware.

code_label: Sequence length increases qubits and depth
text_span: an increase in sequence length results in a linear rise in the number of qubits and the trainable parameters following weight sharing, while concurrently inducing a superlinear escalation in gate depth and complexity.
rationale: Key scalability observation from the resource analysis.

code_label: Weight sharing limits parameter growth
text_span: the weight-sharing mechanism substantially reduces the actual number of parameters
rationale: Describes the parameter-sharing strategy and its effect.

code_label: Training time grows sharply with task size
text_span: for Task 2, approximately 13 min per epoch; for Task 3, approximately 2 h per epoch; and for Task 4, over 6 h per epoch.
rationale: Reports practical computational cost as sequence length increases.

code_label: QNN-SAMo requires least resources
text_span: the analysis indicates that QNN-SAMo requires the least resources, while SAM has the highest parameter count
rationale: Resource comparison across models.

code_label: Future work on preprocessing and quantum-native paradigms
text_span: Exploring the correlation between QNN-SAM performance and data preprocessing methods.
rationale: One of the explicit future research directions.

code_label: Future work on quantum linear algebra
text_span: Establishing a quantum-native paradigm based on quantum arithmetic, such as quantum linear algebra (QLA), to surpass traditional simulation approaches.
rationale: Second explicit future research direction.

code_label: Future work on broader QNNs with SAM
text_span: Developing advanced QNNs that integrate the SAM for a wide range of learning tasks.
rationale: Third explicit future research direction.

code_label: Need for better architecture and noise suppression
text_span: the critical factor still lies in finding an appropriate architecture for the QNN-SAM network to learn the dataset and achieve high accuracy while also possessing strong resistance against quantum noise.
rationale: States a caveat that performance depends on architecture and noise resistance.
